title: Limits Involving Infinity; Asymptotes of Graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Horizontal Asymptote
definitions.latex: \lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = L \quad \text{or} \quad \lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x) = L \implies y = L
definitions.statement: A horizontal line y = L is a horizontal asymptote of the graph of y = f(x) if either lim_{x->oo} f(x) = L or lim_{x->-oo} f(x) = L.
conditions: L must be a finite real number
Evaluated as x grows without bound in either direction
definitions.explanation: Describes end behavior of functions at extreme horizontal distances.
definitions.keyTakeaway: A curve can cross its horizontal asymptote multiple times; it dictates behavior only at infinity.

definitions.title: Vertical Asymptote
definitions.latex: \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = \pm \infty \quad \text{or} \quad \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = \pm \infty \implies x = c
definitions.statement: A vertical line x = c is a vertical asymptote of the graph of y = f(x) if at least one of the one-sided limits of f(x) as x approaches c is +oo or -oo.
conditions: Function values grow unbounded near c
definitions.explanation: Commonly arises at zeroes of the simplified denominator of rational functions.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Vertical asymptotes represent infinite discontinuities where curves diverge.

definitions.title: Degree Comparison Rule for Rational Functions
definitions.latex: f(x) = \frac{a_n x^n + \dots}{b_m x^m + \dots} \implies \lim_{x \to \pm \infty} f(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & n < m \\ \frac{a_n}{b_m}, & n = m \\ \pm \infty, & n > m \end{cases}
definitions.statement: The limit at infinity of a rational function depends entirely on the leading terms of numerator and denominator.
conditions: Degrees n and m are non-negative integers
Leading coefficients an and bm are non-zero
definitions.explanation: Dividing every term by the highest power of x in the denominator reduces lower-order terms to zero.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Higher degree in denominator -> 0; equal degrees -> ratio of leading coefficients.

definitions.title: Oblique (Slant) Asymptote
definitions.statement: If the degree of the numerator of a rational function exceeds the degree of the denominator by exactly 1, polynomial long division yields y = mx + b as an oblique asymptote.
definitions.explanation: The graph approaches the slanted line y = mx + b as |x| becomes large.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Oblique asymptotes occur when numerator degree is exactly one higher than denominator degree.
